enclosures.name: 4x2x2 PVC Enclosure
enclosures.note: Excellent humidity retention for ball pythons

enclosures.name: 4x4x2 PVC Enclosure
enclosures.note: Extra floor space for larger females

heating.name: Halogen Flood Heat Bulb (100w PAR38)
heating.description: Primary heat source — best mimics natural sunlight. ReptiFiles top recommendation.
heating.safetyNote: Must be paired with a thermostat

heating.name: Arcadia Deep Heat Projector
heating.description: Penetrates deeper than surface heat mats. Excellent for ambient heat in large enclosures.

heating.name: Arcadia Optimal Heating Pack (75W Halogen + 50W DHP)
Ceramic Heat Emitter (CHE)
heating.description: No-light heat source, good for maintaining ambient temps at night.

heating.name: Radiant Heat Panel
heating.description: Preferred for large enclosures. Creates large warm zones.

heating.name: Digital Thermostat (Inkbird or Herpstat)
heating.description: Required with ALL heat sources to prevent burns and overheating.
heating.safetyNote: Place probe inside warm hide at snake level — not on heat mat surface

heating.name: Under Tank Heat Mat
heating.description: Supplemental only — helps maintain warm hide temp. NOT sufficient as primary heat source in adult enclosures.
heating.warning: Supplemental use only — must be thermostat controlled

uvb.name: Arcadia T5 HO 6% UVB Bulb
uvb.description: ReptiFiles recommended. Span half the enclosure on warm side. Proven to benefit ball python health.
uvb.note: Place 12-18" from snake. Replace every 12 months.

uvb.name: Zoo Med ReptiSun 6.0 T5 HO
uvb.description: Good alternative UVB option. Span at least half the enclosure length.

uvb.name: No UVB (not recommended)
uvb.description: Ball pythons can survive without UVB but ReptiFiles strongly recommends it for optimal welfare.
uvb.warning: If skipping UVB, ensure calcium supplementation is adequate

substrates.name: DIY Topsoil + ReptiSoil + Play Sand Mix
substrates.description: 40% topsoil + 40% Zoo Med ReptiSoil + 20% play sand. ReptiFiles top recommendation. Excellent humidity retention.
substrates.note: Mix well, soak until muddy, pack firmly, dry overnight before introducing snake

substrates.name: Bio Dude Terra Firma
substrates.description: Premium pre-mixed bioactive substrate. Ideal for bioactive setups.

substrates.name: Zoo Med Eco Earth (Coconut Fiber)
substrates.description: Holds humidity well but can get stuck in heat pits. Better as part of a mix.

substrates.name: Zoo Med Forest Floor Cypress Mulch
substrates.description: Attractive, holds humidity well. Use large pieces to reduce ingestion risk.

substrates.name: Paper Towels / Blue Shop Towels
substrates.description: Quarantine and hatchling use only. Does not hold humidity. Not suitable for adults long-term.

substrates.name: Organic Topsoil (40% of mix — buy at Home Depot/Lowes)
Play Sand 50lb (20% of mix — buy at Home Depot/Lowes)
Zoo Med Eco Earth Coconut Fiber

humidity.name: Exo Terra Pressure Sprayer (2L)
humidity.description: Mist enclosure twice daily (morning and evening). Essential for maintaining 60-80% humidity.

humidity.name: Automatic Misting System (MistKing or Exo Terra)
humidity.description: Best option for consistent humidity. Programmable, hands-free.

humidity.name: Sphagnum Moss (for humid hide)
humidity.description: Line humid hide with damp sphagnum moss. Replace monthly to prevent mold. Most humid spot in enclosure.

humidity.name: Digital Thermometer/Hygrometer
humidity.description: Place humidity probe in middle of enclosure. Target 60-80% ambient, 80-100% in humid hide.

hides.name: Warm Hide (on hot side, 90-95°F)
hides.description: Place directly under or near heat lamp. Snug fit — snake should feel walls touching body.

hides.name: Cool Hide (on cool side, 75-80°F)
hides.description: Required. Ball pythons must always have a retreat on the cool side.

hides.name: Humid Hide (center to cool side)
hides.description: Line with damp sphagnum moss. Most humid spot in enclosure. Critical for healthy shedding.

hides.name: Cork Log / Cork Rounds
hides.description: Additional hides and climbing enrichment. Ball pythons are semi-arboreal and will use these.

hides.name: Sturdy Climbing Branch
hides.description: Ball pythons climb more than many assume. Enrichment improves welfare.

monitoring.name: Etekcity Infrared Temperature Gun
monitoring.description: Most accurate way to monitor surface temps. Check warm hide target: 90-95°F. Cool side: 75-80°F. Essential.

feeding.name: RodentPro Frozen Feeder Small Rats (20 Count)
feeding.description: For juveniles and smaller adults under ~500g. Always feed frozen/thawed — never live. Thaw completely to room temperature before offering.

feeding.name: RodentPro Frozen Feeder Medium Rats (10 Count)
feeding.description: For most adult ball pythons 500g-1500g. Prey width should match the widest part of the snake's body.

feeding.name: RodentPro Frozen Feeder Large Rats (5 Count)
feeding.description: For large adult females over 1500g. A slight bulge after eating is normal and expected.

feeding.name: Lasnten Stainless Steel Feeding Tongs 12
feeding.description: Required for safe feeding. Never hand-feed ball pythons — it trains a bite response. Tongs simulate natural prey movement and keep hands safe.

enclosure.note: Older 40-gallon recommendations are not science-based per ReptiFiles

heatSources.thermostatProbe: Inside warm hide at snake level — NOT on heat mat surface

nonNegotiables: Thermostat required on ALL heat sources
3 hides minimum: warm, cool, and humid
Large soaking water bowl always available
4" minimum substrate depth for humidity retention
